$comment: Contract Verification Results SEP (draft) — the per-verifier status object. Closed for a producer: a document of schema_version 1.0 carries exactly these fields. A consumer validates with additionalProperties relaxed, so a higher MINOR stays readable. Incorporates the Registry API draft (stellar-protocol#1944).
title: Contract Verification Status Object (Results SEP 1.0)
description: The static document at <result-root>/wasms/{wasm_hash}.json, and the body of a verifier's dynamic GET /v1/wasms/{wasm_hash}.json (200 = these bytes; 202 = one unverified entry while a verification is in flight).

schema.description: The document type. Every Results SEP document names its type here beside its version.

schema_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR of this schema, versioned independently of the SEP document. Adding a field is a MINOR; removing or redefining one is a MAJOR. Consumers branch on MAJOR and tolerate a higher MINOR.

wasm_hash.description: The Wasm hash this document is about. Lowercase hex SHA-256.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the last change to this document across all of its entries — a new verification, or an archive reference added to an existing one. The clock a bulk-load consumer synchronises on.

source_code_verifications.description: The verifier's own entry, and only its own: a result root publishes one result per Wasm hash. Keyed by the verifier's identity rather than by position — cross-verifier results are a different document with a different `schema`, and a reader that indexes [0] is correct until the day it is not.

verifier.description: A verifier's identity. Exactly one field identifies: `url`, the result root. `name` is what the verifier calls itself — self-claimed, preferred, never authoritative, and present to be displayed rather than keyed on. A reader that wants a name it can hold someone to derives one from `url` (its certificate, the reader's own list); that is a UI concern and not this document's.

url.description: The verifier's result root, and its identity. Two entries in one document, or two members of any set of verifiers built on it, cannot share it: the same result root IS the same verifier. Compared after normalising: scheme and host lowercased, one trailing `/` dropped, path kept and case-sensitive — without a stated rule two implementations disagree on whether `https://v.example/` and `https://v.example` are one verifier or two.

name.description: Self-claimed. Display it, do not key on it, and do not read it as an endorsement by whoever relayed it.

result_url.description: A link to a published artifact. `sha256` is REQUIRED on every entry pointing at content the publishing verifier controls — the report and any archive copy of it.

type.description: What the link points at — a content-category axis.

location.description: Where the link's bytes live — a storage-location axis, independent of `type`. Two entries can share a `type` (this verifier's own copy and the Arweave copy of the same report) and differ only in `location`.

source_code_uri.description: Where THIS verifier serves a retrievable copy of the source that produced the match. No `type`: every entry is the same kind of thing, so `location` alone distinguishes them. No `sha256`: the entry's parent already carries `source_sha256` over the same bytes.

status.description: verified: the rebuild reproduced the deployed bytes; mismatched: it did not (rebuilt_hash carries what it produced); unverified: no result — the 202 body while a verification is in flight, or an aggregator's placeholder for a verifier with none. A consumer treats an unrecognised value as unverified.

recipe_source.description: Where the build recipe came from: SEP-58 fields carried in the contract's SEP-46 meta, or the submitter.

image_trust_level.description: How the build environment came about: an image the official Stellar pipeline publishes; composed by the verifier from pinned official components; digest-pinned with a public reproducible definition; digest-pinned with provenance not established.

bldarg.description: SEP-58 v0.6.0: leading entry-point arguments. ORDER IS SIGNIFICANT; never sorted. Absent AND empty both mean SEP-58's default, `contract build` — a consumer must not read `[]` as an empty argument vector (see the SEP's status-object section).

bldopt.description: SEP-58: build options, one complete flag per entry in `--flag=value` form. Order is not significant.

source_sha256.description: SEP-58: SHA-256 of the source archive the verification was produced from.

source_uri.description: SEP-58: where the archive can be fetched. Scheme is open-ended.

verified_source_code_uris.description: Where THIS verifier serves a retrievable copy of the source that produced the match.

rebuilt_hash.description: The hash the rebuild produced. Present exactly when status is mismatched.

results_urls.description: Links to what this verifier published for this verification: at least the report. Appended to over time (an archive copy arriving), never reset.

allOf.$comment: The verdict-conditional fields are present exactly when the entry carries a verdict.

then.$comment: An unverified entry is exactly {verifier, status} — not merely one missing the four verdict-conditional fields. Nothing has been published yet, so no recipe, no custody, no build inputs and no links have a value; listing only the four left `bldimg`/`bldopt`/`results_urls` legal on an entry that by definition has none.

allOf.$comment: rebuilt_hash is present exactly when status is mismatched.
